programs.indication: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH): a fatty-liver disease in which fat buildup causes liver inflammation and cell damage, and which can progress toward cirrhosis.
programs.drug_mechanism: An oral, once-daily small-molecule drug that selectively activates the thyroid hormone receptor-beta (a liver-cell receptor that helps regulate fat and cholesterol metabolism).
programs.phase: Phase 2 completed (week-12 and week-36 data reported); Phase 3 planned
programs.ownership_partner: Wholly owned by the company; no partner disclosed in the eligible sources
programs.design: Randomized 2:1 (drug:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center, about 25 U.S. sites [c13]

sample_sizes.note: exact planned-vs-enrolled distinction not separately stated in the eligible sources [c13]

programs.treatment_duration: 36 weeks, with an optional 36-week extension for some patients
programs.primary_endpoint: Relative reduction in liver fat content at week 12, measured by MRI-PDFF (a non-invasive MRI method that estimates the fraction of fat in the liver)
programs.secondary_endpoints: Liver fat reduction sustained to week 36; NASH resolution on liver biopsy; a >2-point improvement in the NAFLD Activity Score (a biopsy-based severity score); fibrosis change; normalization of the liver enzyme ALT; lipid changes

latest_evidence.week12_primary: 36.3% liver-fat reduction overall (42.0% in a pre-specified high-exposure subgroup) vs 9.6% for placebo, p<0.0001 [c14]
latest_evidence.fibrosis: Resolved in 50% of drug-treated patients who achieved NASH resolution; >=1-point reduction in 29% of drug-treated vs 23% of placebo patients [c16]
latest_evidence.ALT: Significantly more normalization in drug-treated than placebo patients [c17]
latest_evidence.safety: Mostly mild-to-moderate adverse events, balanced between arms; mild loose stools at treatment start in the drug arm [c18]
latest_evidence.missing: No confidence intervals were stated in the eligible sources for the percentage effect sizes above; only p-values were given.

programs.management_says_vs_regulator_says: Management said the NASH-resolution result 'suggests a high likelihood of success' in a similarly designed, longer Phase 3 trial and described NASH resolution as 'an approvable FDA endpoint' [c12]. No independent regulator statement is in the eligible packet; the company itself said the Phase 3 design was still 'pending regulatory agreement' as of the cutoff [c12].
programs.next_milestone: Planned start of a Phase 3 trial, guided for late 2018 or early 2019, subject to regulatory agreement on design; announced 2018-11-06 [c6]
programs.economic_relevance: Pre-revenue; this is the company's primary value driver. The company said its cash position was significant relative to its currently planned Phase 3 programs, but gave no specific trial-cost figure [c7].

unresolved_questions: Whether the regulator will agree to the proposed pivotal-trial design for the primary indication, and on what timeline, given that agreement had not been publicly confirmed as of the cutoff.
Whether the week-12 and week-36 imaging- and biopsy-based results from a 125-patient Phase 2 trial will replicate in a larger, longer pivotal trial.
How the company will prioritize and fund development of the second (cholesterol-disorder) indication alongside the primary liver-disease program.

own: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial met its week-12 primary endpoint (liver-fat reduction) with p<0.0001, and the effect was sustained through week 36 [c14][c15].

36-week liver-biopsy data showed statistically significant NASH resolution (27% vs 6.5% placebo, p=0.02) and fibrosis improvement, endpoints management described as approvable by regulators [c3][c16][c12].

The company holds $488.5 million in cash and investments against about 15.4 million shares outstanding and no debt line items found in the structured financial data, which management called significant relative to its planned Phase 3 programs [c4][c9][c21][c7].
flat: Regulatory agreement on the proposed pivotal Phase 3 trial design had not been publicly confirmed as of the cutoff; the company itself described it as 'pending' [c12].

The Phase 2 population was small (125 enrolled; as few as 34 placebo patients had paired week-36 biopsies), so effect sizes in a larger, longer Phase 3 trial are not established by this data alone [c13][c3].
short: The results getting the most attention (NASH resolution, fibrosis change) are secondary, biopsy-based endpoints from a small trial; the company has not secured regulatory agreement on how to run a confirmatory trial, and that trial's cost is not yet disclosed [c3][c12][c7].
Nearly all of the year's large cash increase came from a June 2018 stock sale rather than from operations, and the company is pre-revenue with no approved product [c8][c5].

scene.setup_label: A friend sends you a stock tip.
scene.voice: Their liver-disease drug cut liver fat in a placebo-controlled trial and the biopsies show the disease actually resolving. They just raised close to half a billion, and the plenary slot at the big liver meeting says the field is paying attention.

scene.question: Is a strong Phase 2 in a small trial, with the pivotal design still pending regulatory agreement, worth today's price?

ask_friend.a: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 of 125 patients [c13]. Liver fat fell 36% at week 12 against placebo, p<0.0001, and 37% versus 8.9% at week 36 [c14][c15]. On biopsy, NASH resolved in 27% of treated patients against 6.5% on placebo, p=0.02, and fibrosis improved in half of those [c3][c16]. Side effects were mild and balanced [c18]. The caveats: biopsy endpoints are secondary, the placebo arm with paired biopsies was small, and the pivotal-trial design is still pending agreement with the regulator [c12].

Cash and investments were $488.5 million at 30 September, up from $191.5 million, after a June stock sale that raised about $283 million [c4][c8]. Shares outstanding rose from 14.2 million to 15.4 million [c9]. Revenue is zero [c5]. At the recent operating outflow of about $6.4 million a quarter the runway looks very long, but that rate predates a 900-patient Phase 3, which management says it plans to start in late 2018 or early 2019 and believes it can fund [c6][c7][c11].

ask_friend.q: How much is already in the price?
ask_friend.a: The last close is $186.51, up more than 300% over twelve months but 41% below the 12-month high. Market capitalisation is about $2.9 billion with about $482 million of net cash [c10]; no revenue, so no multiple. A second programme in an inherited cholesterol disorder has a completed Phase 2 and no Phase 3 plan yet [c19][c20]. The price is paying for a Phase 3 that has not started in a disease where Phase 2 signals have often failed to replicate.

claims.text: The company presented 36-week Phase 2 liver-biopsy and lipid data for its lead liver-disease drug at a hepatology-conference plenary session on 12 Nov 2018.
The trial's week-12 primary-endpoint result (liver fat reduction by MRI-PDFF, p<0.0001) was already public in company disclosures by 13 Mar 2018.
36-week results -- NASH resolution 27% vs 6.5% placebo (p=0.02) and a >2-point NAFLD Activity Score improvement in 56% vs 32% of patients (p=0.02) -- were first announced 31 May 2018.
Cash and investments were $488.5 million at 30 Sep 2018, up from $191.5 million at 31 Dec 2017.
Total revenue was $0 for both the three- and nine-month periods ended 30 Sep 2018.

Management said it expected to begin a Phase 3 study in the primary liver-disease indication in late 2018 or early 2019, subject to regulatory approval, and said it was evaluating the design of a possible Phase 3 study in the related cholesterol-disorder indication that could begin in 2019.
Management said it believed it had significant financial resources to fund its currently planned Phase 3 programs.

In June 2018 the company completed an underwritten public offering of common stock, issuing 983,607 new company shares (plus shares sold by selling stockholders), with net proceeds to the company of about $282.8 million for general corporate purposes including R&D and clinical-trial costs.
Common shares outstanding rose from 14,227,634 at 31 Dec 2017 to 15,393,309 at 30 Sep 2018.
Net cash (cash and investments of $488.538 million minus total liabilities of $6.642 million) was about $481.9 million at 30 Sep 2018.

At the nine-month 2018 average quarterly cash-outflow rate from operations (about $6.41 million/quarter), the reported cash and investments balance would cover roughly 19 years before financing or spending patterns change -- a scenario, not a company forecast, and one that ignores the funding needs of the newly planned Phase 3 programs.

The company described the proposed pivotal-trial design for the primary indication as pending regulatory agreement, and did not disclose a completed regulator agreement on trial design as of the cutoff.

The trial (NCT02912260) enrolled 125 patients in a randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center design across about 25 U.S. sites; 73 drug-treated and 34 placebo patients had paired baseline/week-36 biopsies.
At week 12, liver fat was reduced 36.3% in drug-treated patients overall (42.0% in a pre-specified high-exposure subgroup) versus 9.6% for placebo (p<0.0001).
The liver-fat reduction was sustained at week 36: 37% for drug-treated patients versus 8.9% for placebo (p<0.0001).

Among drug-treated patients who achieved NASH resolution on biopsy, fibrosis also resolved in 50% of cases; overall, at least a one-point fibrosis reduction occurred in 29% of drug-treated versus 23% of placebo patients.
Significantly more drug-treated than placebo patients had normalization of a liver enzyme (ALT) associated with liver injury.
Adverse events were mostly mild to moderate and balanced between drug and placebo arms; mild loose stools were reported at the start of treatment in the drug-treated group.

In a separate, previously completed 116-patient Phase 2 trial in the related inherited high-cholesterol disorder, the drug produced an 18.8% placebo-corrected reduction in LDL cholesterol (p<0.0001), and 21% in patients on an optimal dose.
The company said it was evaluating the design and objectives of a possible Phase 3 study in the cholesterol-disorder indication that could begin in 2019.

No debt-related financial-statement line item (e.g., notes payable, long-term debt) appears in the structured (XBRL) data for fiscal 2017 or the first three quarters of 2018, and no interest expense was reported for those periods; the small liabilities balance ($6.6 million at 30 Sep 2018) appears to be short-term operating liabilities.
